meta.titre: Subject-Verb Agreement: finding the true subject and matching the verb

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A school notice in Bamenda reads, "The list of successful candidates, together with their addresses, is on the board." A careless reader sees "candidates" next to the verb and expects "are". The writer, however, knows that the list is the subject. Paper 1 of the Advanced Level English examination keeps testing exactly this kind of choice, because the nearest noun is rarely the one that decides the verb. This lesson shows you how to find the real subject every time.

items: A subject is the person or thing that does the action or is described; the verb is the word that tells what it does or is.
Singular means one and plural means more than one; most plural nouns end in -s.
The verb *be* has the forms am, is, are, was, were; the verb *have* has *has* and *have*.

sections.titre: Matching the verb to its true subject
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The basic rule

A verb agrees in number with its subject. A singular subject takes a singular verb (*the pupil writes, is, has, was*) and a plural subject takes a plural verb (*the pupils write, are, have, were*). Always find the real subject first: it is the noun that the sentence is about, not the noun nearest to the verb.

### Rules that examination questions test

| Situation | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Words between subject and verb | They do not change the verb. | *The box of oranges is on the table.* |
| *with, together with, as well as, along with, in addition to* | They add information but do not make the subject plural. | *The captain, together with his players, is training.* |
| Subjects joined by *and* | Plural verb. | *Ayuk and Ngwa are cousins.* |
| *and* joining one idea, or *each* / *every* before the subjects | Singular verb. | *Bread and butter is a simple breakfast. Every boy and girl has a seat.* |
| *either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also* | The verb agrees with the nearer subject. | *Either the manager or the clerks are to sign.* |
| *each, every, everyone, nobody, someone, either, neither, one* | Singular. | *Each of the girls has a pen.* |
| *both, few, many, several* | Plural. | *Many were late.* |
| *all, some, most, half* + *of* | The noun after *of* decides. | *Some of the water is dirty. Some of the pupils are late.* |
| Collective nouns (team, committee, class) | Singular when the group acts as one body. | *The committee has reached a decision.* |
| *news, mathematics, physics, economics* | Singular although they end in -s. | *Physics is taught on Mondays.* |
| *scissors, trousers, police, cattle, people* | Plural. | *The police are on the road.* |
| Sums, distances, periods of time | Singular when seen as one amount. | *Five years is a long time.* |
| *a number of* / *the number of* | A number of + plural verb; the number of + singular verb. | *A number of pupils are absent. The number of pupils is small.* |
| *there is / there are* | The verb agrees with the noun that follows. | *There are three chairs.* |

### Lists after a dash

A subject may be followed by a list set off with dashes or commas that explains it. The list does not change the number of the subject: *The joy of teaching - its rewards, its frustrations, its surprises - is hard to describe.* The verb agrees with *joy*.

### Relative pronouns

*Who, which* and *that* take the number of the noun they replace: *the pupils who sit at the back are ...*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the subjects are joined by either ... or, neither ... nor, or not only ... but also
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look at the subject placed just before the verb. *Neither the nurse nor the doctors were present* has a plural verb because *doctors* is nearer. If the order changes, the verb changes too: *Neither the doctors nor the nurse was present*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a long phrase or clause stands between the subject and the verb
variantes.contenu_markdown: Cross out every phrase set off by commas or dashes and every phrase that begins with *of, in, at, with* or *as well as*. Read the sentence again with only the remaining subject and verb, decide singular or plural, then put the phrases back.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the subject is a pronoun such as each, neither, none of them or a quantity word such as a number of
variantes.contenu_markdown: *Each, every, either, neither* and *one* are singular even when followed by *of* and a plural noun: *Neither of the two answers is correct*. *Both, few, many* and *several* are always plural. With *all, some, most* and *half*, look at the noun after *of*.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Choose the option that completes the sentence correctly.

The quality of the mangoes sold at the town market, as well as their low prices, ______ attracting buyers from far away.

A) are   B) is   C) were   D) have been

etapes.action: Mark the verb position and find the subject.
etapes.justification: The subject answers the question *what is attracting buyers?* The nouns *mangoes*, *market* and *prices* are all inside side phrases, and *quality* is the head noun.
The phrases *of the mangoes sold at the town market* and *as well as their low prices* give extra information. *As well as* does not join two subjects into a plural one.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Reduced sentence: *The quality ______ attracting buyers from far away.*

etapes.action: Decide the number and the tense.
etapes.justification: *Quality* is singular. The word *attracting* needs a form of *be* for a continuous action happening now, so a present form is needed and *were* (past) does not fit.

etapes.action: Test the options on the reduced sentence.
etapes.justification: *Are* and *have been* are plural. *Were* is a plural past form. Only *is* agrees with *quality*.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A) no; B) yes; C) no; D) no.

etapes.action: Read the full sentence aloud with the chosen verb.
etapes.justification: The full sentence must sound natural once the phrases return.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *The quality of the mangoes sold at the town market, as well as their low prices, is attracting buyers from far away.*

sections.conclusion_markdown: **B) is.** The side phrases introduced by *of* and *as well as* do not change the number of the true subject *quality*.

items.erreur_markdown: *The box of oranges are on the table.*
items.pourquoi_faux: The verb has been attracted to the nearest noun, *oranges*, but the subject is *box*.
items.correction_markdown: *The box of oranges is on the table.*

items.erreur_markdown: *Each of the girls have a prize.*
items.pourquoi_faux: *Each* is singular even when *of* and a plural noun follow it.
items.correction_markdown: *Each of the girls has a prize.*

items.erreur_markdown: *Neither the manager nor the clerks is present.*
items.pourquoi_faux: With *neither ... nor*, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, and *clerks* is plural.
items.correction_markdown: *Neither the manager nor the clerks are present.*

items.pourquoi_faux: *News* ends in -s but takes a singular verb.

items.erreur_markdown: *The police is looking for the thief.*
items.pourquoi_faux: *Police* is plural in meaning (the police officers) and takes a plural verb.
items.correction_markdown: *The police are looking for the thief.*

items.enonce_markdown:
Choose the correct word.

(a) The pupils in Form Two (is / are) making a model.
(b) Everybody (was / were) happy with the prize.
(c) The scissors on the shelf (is / are) blunt.
(d) Physics (is / are) taught on Mondays.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **are** (plural subject *pupils*).
(b) **was** (*everybody* is singular).
(c) **are** (*scissors* is plural).
(d) **is** (*physics* is singular).

items.enonce_markdown:
Complete each sentence with the present form of *be*.

(a) A number of farmers ______ waiting outside the cooperative.
(b) The number of farmers in the village ______ rising.
(c) Either the chairman or the members ______ to sign the book.
(d) Ten thousand FCFA ______ too much to pay for that book.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **are**: *a number of* takes a plural verb.
(b) **is**: *the number of* takes a singular verb.
(c) **are**: the nearer subject *members* is plural.
(d) **is**: the sum is thought of as one amount.

items.enonce_markdown:
Correct the sentences. One sentence is already correct; identify it.

(a) The list of required books, which includes two novels and a dictionary, are on the notice board.
(b) Neither of the two answers are correct.
(c) There is three candidates waiting outside.
(d) Every student and teacher have to sign the register.
(e) The committee has reached its decision.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **is**: the subject is *list*; the relative clause does not change it.
(b) **is**: *neither* is singular.
(c) **There are three candidates**: the verb agrees with *candidates*.
(d) **has**: *every* before the joined subjects makes the verb singular.
(e) **Correct**: *committee* acts as one body.

items_markdown: Find the true subject first; ignore phrases introduced by *of*, *with*, *together with* and *as well as*.
*Either ... or* and *neither ... nor* make the verb agree with the nearer subject.
*Each, every, either, neither* and *one* are singular, even before *of* and a plural noun; *both, few, many, several* are plural.
*A number of* takes a plural verb but *the number of* takes a singular verb.
*News, mathematics, physics* are singular; *scissors, police, people* are plural.
A list after a dash explains the subject and does not make it plural.
